stem: Which one of the following statements about cell counts in CSF is correct?

options.text: In a clear tap, normal CSF contains some white cells
Neonates are an exception where polymorphs can be present in the CSF without mononuclear cells
The white cell count in viral meningitis is predominantly composed of mononuclear cells and few polymorphs
In a traumatic tap, where there might be blood staining of the CSF a clinician uses a ratio of one white cell to every thousand red cells to calculate the significance of white cells in the CSF
The turbidity of normal CSF varies with posture

explanation: Viral meningitis typically causes a lymphocytic (mononuclear) pleocytosis, often with only a few polymorphs. Normal CSF should not contain white cells in a clear tap, and traumatic tap correction is not based on a fixed 1:1000 ratio.

optionExplanations.A: Normal CSF in a clear tap should have no white cells.
optionExplanations.B: This is not a standard feature of neonatal CSF interpretation.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: viral meningitis usually shows predominantly mononuclear cells with fewer polymorphs.
optionExplanations.D: Traumatic tap correction does not use a fixed 1 WCC per 1000 RBC rule.
optionExplanations.E: CSF turbidity is not expected to vary with posture in normal physiology.
